segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'The driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of w2 bounds separately.

'a person riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device, read as the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency), as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1.

Reuses the index mapping of 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.' (NRS_484B_270_1): the three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, never expanded into class atoms.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the rider, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user b other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter and moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance; a rider at rest is not read.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a riding bicyclist or scooter rider; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moving car closes on a bicycle riding ahead in the same lane; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance and the car does not slow.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car slows behind the moving bicycle and keeps a closest approach beyond p.conflict_centre_clearance, then passes with a wide berth; no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is an electric scooter (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding near a bicycle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moving car passes alongside a riding electric bicycle with no conflicting closest approach; contact between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moving car drives on an empty street: no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
